label: For any proposition someone knows it; someone knows every truth
term: for any proposition someone knows it; someone knows every truth
resolution: Literal step2 lacks a truth guard; contextual reading inherits it from step1/final every-truth scope. Separate sibling claims preserve both without equivalence. On either reading step3 is an explicit common-knower bridge, not valid by exchanging per-proposition existential witnesses. Possible/actual knowledge, factivity/closure and world scope require independent treatment; no God/necessary/rigid knower is inferred. Declaration completion binds only the actual per-content antecedents for senses _2 and _3. Sense _1 remains unresolved: its definition collects possible knowledge, actual per-truth witnesses and a common witness as a scope family, rather than specifying one completed sense. Proposed split preserving its identity and links: retain the original as the scope-family record; separate truth-guarded possible knowledge (step1), actual per-truth knowledge (reuse sense _3), and common truth-knower (steps3–4). A possible-knowledge sibling still needs an explicit world/accessibility and agent-domain interpretation; no fixed-agent epistemic operator supplies the missing agent quantifier. No conjunction of these commitments is asserted.
